comment: The intake rubric — the engine behind the quality gate on the first screen a requester sees. Three layers. The FLOOR is heuristic and deterministic: it catches a name, a fragment, or keyboard noise with no model call. The SCORING layer is the only part a model touches, and it does exactly one thing — assign 0, 1 or 2 per dimension against the anchors below, strictly on the presence of factual detail and never on length. Everything downstream is deterministic: the pass rule, and the feedback string for that dimension at that score. Feedback is verbatim business copy — edit it here, never in code. FAIL OPEN: if the model is unavailable or wrong, intake proceeds. A quality assistant that blocks submission has become a gate, and the mission is reducing friction.

engine.opening: Thanks — this is enough to start. A few more specifics would let the platform route this properly and save you questions later:

messages.tooShort: That is too thin to work from. A few sentences about what the activity does, what data it touches and who else is involved gives the platform something to route on — and saves you being asked later.
messages.notProse: That does not read as a description yet. The platform routes on what you write, so it needs real sentences about the activity.

anchors.0: No indication of what the activity actually does.
anchors.1: Names a system or a category, but not the business function it serves.
anchors.2: Names the activity and states the specific business process it supports.

feedback.0: What it does: describe what this actually does, in one sentence. For example, "it proposes which queue an incoming insurance claim should go to".
feedback.1: What it does: you have named the system — what business process does it support? The specific job it does, rather than the category it belongs to.

starters.label: Automates an internal process…
starters.insert: It automates our internal process of

starters.label: Supports a decision…
starters.insert: It analyses data to support decisions about

starters.label: Customer-facing service…
starters.insert: It is a customer-facing service that lets customers

anchors.1: Mentions data without saying what kind, or how sensitive.
anchors.2: Names the kinds of data involved and whether any of it identifies people.

feedback.0: Data: what data does this hold or read? Naming it — customer records, employee details, financial transactions — decides which questions you are asked.
feedback.1: Data: you have mentioned data. Does any of it identify a person, or count as confidential? That is what changes the questions.

starters.label: Personal data about customers…
starters.insert: It processes personal data about customers, specifically

starters.label: No personal data
starters.insert: It holds no personal data — only

anchors.0: Says nothing about suppliers, partners or other teams.
anchors.1: Alludes to someone outside without naming them or their role.
anchors.2: Names the supplier or partner and what they do in the activity.

feedback.0: Who else: is anyone outside the organisation involved — a supplier, a platform, a partner? Naming them here saves the third-party questions being asked cold.
feedback.1: Who else: you have mentioned someone external. Who are they, and what do they actually do in this activity?

starters.label: Built and run in-house
starters.insert: It is built and run entirely in-house, with no external supplier involved.

anchors.0: Says nothing about where it runs or where data sits.
anchors.2: States where it runs and where the data sits.

feedback.0: Where it runs: is this in our environment, a supplier's, or somewhere else? Where the data sits changes who has to review it.
feedback.1: Where it runs: you have said it is hosted — whose environment, and where does the data sit?

starters.label: In our own environment
starters.insert: It runs in our own environment, with data held in

starters.label: In the supplier's environment…
starters.insert: It runs in the supplier's environment, with data held in
